summary: No Riau Islands-specific law, enforcement action, institution or documented incident was identified in the source inventory. The province shows no divergence from Indonesia's national framework, and the national assessment applies to visitors here without regional qualification.
tangentialFactors: Enforcement of morality and public-order provisions varies between Indonesian localities rather than following a single national pattern. In one 2020 raid, detainees were released because no regional regulation existed to charge them under; the source does not identify the locality, so the case cannot be attributed to the Riau Islands and is recorded only as evidence that provincial and municipal regulation, not national statute alone, determines outcomes in a given place.
localsOnly: No resident-facing finding specific to the Riau Islands was identified. Trans residents of the province are governed by the same national rules on legal gender recognition, expression and morality offences that apply elsewhere in Indonesia, and the inventory records no provincial regulation, court practice or local protection mechanism that adds to or relieves those rules.
outOfScopeNotes: No sourcing was found on provincial or municipal regulations in the Riau Islands that would supplement or derogate from the national framework, and none on how enforcement is practised in Batam, Tanjung Pinang or the smaller islands. Whether the absence of a regional morality regulation, as seen in the 2020 raid case, holds across the province is unresolved.
